phase3_findings.description: Request-time catalog check (_check_catalog_blocking / ensure_catalog_confirmed) has no read/write or statement timeout and runs under the process-wide state.lock, so a stalled information_schema read hangs every later rule-set request instead of refusing it with REFUSED_CATALOG_UNCONFIRMED; preflight catalog read has the same gap (startup only).
_rule_set_file_configured returns False silently on unreadable or malformed TOML, so verify-memory skips its rule-sets-unsupported message (still exits 2 with the config error).
Live MySQL refusal cases for INFORMATION_SCHEMA tables and JSON_TABLE use SELECT *, so the whole-row guard refuses them first and the rule-set guard's own refusal is never exercised end to end.
Frozen rule-set records hold mutable lists and LoadedRuleSets is a mutable dataclass; invariants are enforced only by convention after validation.
CatalogConfirmation.confirmed is a public mutable flag set directly by outside code (preflight.py:175).
RuleSetsConfig can hold a file path with _loaded None; consumers check loaded, so a non-validated construction fails open.
RuleSetSelection does not enforce its invariants (positive user_id, known set, bound account); only select_rule_set does.

## Verdict: REJECT (one Important finding: the request-time catalog check can hang rule-set requests)

The PR is not ready to merge: one Important error-handling gap in the new request-time catalog check can make rule-set requests hang with no error instead of being refused.
Rule applied: rule 3 — a Phase-3 finding at or above the threshold → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

### 🟠 Important / Major

1. `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 531-568: the request-time catalog check has no read timeout, and it holds a process-wide lock while it runs. `_check_catalog_blocking` opens its connection with only `connect_timeout=5`, with no `read_timeout`, `write_timeout` or session statement timeout. `ensure_catalog_confirmed` runs it under `state.lock` through `run_blocking_sql`, which limits only the wait for a worker slot. A stalled `information_schema` read, for example a network stall or a metadata lock, therefore blocks with no time limit and ignores `database.statement_timeout_ms`. Every later rule-set request then waits on that lock, so no request gets the `REFUSED_CATALOG_UNCONFIRMED` error. This applies while the check is unconfirmed: under `--no-preflight`, and after a failed check. The preflight catalog read in `preflight.py` (`_check_rule_set_catalog` through `probe_database`) has the same gap, but there it only delays startup. (raised by 1/6 agents)

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (14)

<details><summary>14 items</summary>

1. `src/sqllens/cli.py` lines 98-116: `_rule_set_file_configured` returns `False` without logging on `OSError`, `UnicodeDecodeError` or `TOMLDecodeError`. So when the config file is unreadable or malformed, `verify-memory` prints only the config error and skips its "does not support rule sets" message. The command still exits 2 and names the cause. (raised by 1/6 agents)
2. `tests/connectors/test_rule_sets_mysql.py` lines 421-427: the live MySQL refusal cases for the four `INFORMATION_SCHEMA` tables and for `JSON_TABLE` all use `SELECT *`. The whole-row guard is on by default in `_chain`, so it refuses these first, and the test asserts only `UnsafeSqlError`. The rule-set guard's own catalog and `JSON_TABLE` refusals are therefore never checked end to end. The unit tests in `tests/unit/test_safety_rule_sets.py` do check them directly. (raised by 1/6 agents)
3. `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 77-265: the records use `frozen=True` but hold mutable lists, for example `Binding.account_ids`, `TableRule.columns`, `TableRule.predicate_columns`, `RuleSet.tables` and `RuleSetFile.rule_sets`. These lists can be changed in place after validation, and nothing checks the invariants again. `LoadedRuleSets` is a plain mutable dataclass that is shared for the whole process. (raised by 1/6 agents)
4. `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 234-239: `CatalogConfirmation.confirmed` is a public mutable flag next to its lock. Other code sets it directly, for example `preflight.py:175`, so any caller could mark the catalog as confirmed without running the check. (raised by 1/6 agents)
5. `src/sqllens/config.py` lines 760-828: a `RuleSetsConfig` can have `file` set while `_loaded` is `None`. Every consumer checks `loaded is not None`, so a config built without `Config` validation, for example with `model_construct`, would treat rule sets as off. This fails open. Every current production path goes through validation. (raised by 1/6 agents)
6. `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 348-358: `RuleSetSelection` does not enforce its own invariants, such as a positive `user_id`, a set name that exists and a bound account. Only `select_rule_set` checks them, and `user_key` is the conversation-owner identity. (raised by 1/6 agents)
